findings.headline: Sickest panel in the screen, but 99215 share is about 2x peers at every complexity level; charts show some billing above what was documented
findings.interpretation: Expected 99215 share is 8.7% (sick panel), but at 29.8% it is still above peers in every condition stratum (46% vs 24% at 5+ conditions). Random sample of 30 charts: 4 documented below billed (13%), including 2 of 5 99215s (40% vs 4.5% for all providers). Draft overpayment estimate is $9,829 (CI $1,446 to $18,212). The hybrid chart rule did not trigger because there are too few documented 99215s. This is the top priority for a larger 99215-focused chart review. It is not a finding yet.

findings.headline: Highest risk-adjusted score (15.5); 72% of 99215s are on patients with 0 or 1 conditions, but sampled charts support the levels billed
findings.interpretation: 99215 share is about 24% even for patients with no chronic conditions (peers 2.3%), with diagnoses like URI, UTI and rash. That claims pattern is the classic concern. But all 30 random charts supported the level billed (5 of 5 99215s high MDM). Only 3 of 22 notes describing data review lack a matching lab on the claim, so the claims do not clearly show inflated notes. Charts and claims disagree. Recommend a targeted 99215 chart review of the low-complexity claims.

findings.headline: Highest-volume outlier (2,423 claims, about 344 excess 99215s); charts largely support billing
findings.interpretation: Elevated across all strata. 1 of 30 random charts was below billed, and the 99215s sampled were supported with high MDM and 44 to 48 minutes. The claims signal is strong but chart evidence does not support upcoding. Needs a targeted 99215 review before any conclusion.
